log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Opponent's team: Garchomp, Kingambit, Gholdengo, Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, Volcarona. Their main threats look like Volcarona (fire/bug special), Dragonite, and Gholdengo. Plan: Incineroar leads to use Fake Out and Intimidate. Garchomp (Mega) is the main sweeper; Earthquake hits Steel types like Kingambit and Gholdengo. Gholdengo covers Dragonite and Rotom-Wash with Thunderbolt and Make It Rain. Watch Volcarona's Quiver Dance and Kingambit's Supreme Overlord.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing team composition against their likely threats like Volcarona, Dragonite, and Gholdengo, considering which three of my own Pokémon—Incineroar, Garchomp, Gholdengo, Sinistcha, Corviknight, or Dragapult—give me the best matchup.

I'll settle on leading with Incineroar, then Garchomp, then Gholdengo as my chosen trio.

decisions.thought: Brought Garchomp (lead, mega), Gholdengo (scarf), Kingambit. Opp threats: Dragapult (fast, likely outspeeds), Corviknight (walls Chomp's EQ), Incineroar (intimidate). Gholdengo scarf hits Dragapult/Gholdengo with Shadow Ball. Kingambit uses Sucker Punch on fast Ghosts. Track opp moves, items, and speed.

Opponent's Garchomp is at -1 Atk from Intimidate. Its ability is sandveil or roughskin, and its item is unknown. Opponent also has Kingambit, Gholdengo, Dragonite, Rotom-Wash and Volcarona. My plan: Fake Out now to flinch Garchomp. Then bring in Mega Garchomp (garchompite) for Swords Dance sweeping, with Gholdengo covering Dragonite and Rotom-Wash. Watch Volcarona's Quiver Dance and Kingambit's Supreme Overlord.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Fake Out on Garchomp seems like the right opening move since it's already been hit by Intimidate - it'll flinch and I don't need to worry much about Rough Skin recoil. I'll go with Fake Out and figure out the follow-up after seeing what happens.

decisions.thought: Mega'd Garchomp T1 and EQ'd Incineroar (I'm at -1 from Intimidate). Mega Chomp is a bit slower, still faster than Incineroar. Watch for Fake Out, Will-O-Wisp or Parting Shot. Corviknight walls EQ, so use Stone Edge on it. Dragapult is fast: answer with Kingambit's Sucker Punch or scarf Gholdengo's Shadow Ball.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing Garchomp's options at -1 against Incineroar's likely moves like Fake Out or Will-O-Wisp, then calculating Mega Garchomp's Earthquake damage using its boosted 170 base Attack reduced by the stat drop.

Running the numbers, Mega EQ should land around 161-190 damage, likely chunking Incineroar hard even if not a clean OHKO. Mega Garchomp's speed drops slightly but stays above Incineroar's, so Earthquake looks like the right call here.

decisions.thought: Opponent's Mega Garchomp (Sand Force) is at 87% with -1 Atk. Parting Shot lowers its Atk and SpA and brings in my Garchomp, which outspeeds it and can Mega Evolve and Swords Dance next turn. Gholdengo is weak to Earthquake, so I'd rather not bring it in here. Watch for Kingambit's Supreme Overlord, Volcarona's Quiver Dance, and Dragonite.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar is at full health against Mega Garchomp at 87% with its attack lowered. Since Mega Garchomp is Dragon/Ground with Sand Force, Flare Blitz would be resisted, so I need to weigh my move options carefully given the type matchup.

I'm weighing Protect to scout, Flare Blitz despite the resist, or Parting Shot to pivot into Gholdengo or my own Garchomp. Gholdengo would take heavy Earthquake damage being Steel-type, but switching into my own Garchomp lets me stack another Attack drop on the opponent via Parting Shot and set up a potential Mega Garchomp sweep with Swords Dance since my Garchomp's speed outpaces theirs.

I'll go with Parting Shot.

decisions.thought: Brought Garchomp (Mega'd, lead), scarf Gholdengo, Kingambit. Incineroar has Intimidate and Fake Out (Chomp is at -1). Expect Parting Shot, Will-O-Wisp or a switch. Corviknight walls EQ, so Stone Edge it. Answer fast Dragapult with Sucker Punch or scarf Shadow Ball. Mega Chomp at 158 Spe outspeeds Incineroar.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: I'm estimating Earthquake's damage against Incineroar at roughly 85% of its health, strong enough to threaten it even through Intimidate, and weighing whether Incineroar pivots out with Parting Shot or burns me with Will-O-Wisp instead of trading hits, plus considering how switching to Kingambit interacts with the Intimidate drop.

decisions.thought: Parting Shot brought in my Garchomp. Opposing Mega Garchomp (sandforce, probably Earthquake user) is at 87% with -2 Atk and -1 SpA, so its physical hits are weak. My Garchomp (169 Spe) should outspeed it, so Mega Evolve and Swords Dance or Earthquake next. Gholdengo is weak to Earthquake, so keep it in back. Still unseen: Kingambit (Supreme Overlord), Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, Volcarona (Quiver Dance). Incineroar has Sitrus Berry used and is low, so keep it back.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 84/202 and got forced out by Parting Shot, with only Garchomp or Gholdengo left to switch into against the weakened Mega Garchomp. I'm weighing whether my own Garchomp, being Dragon/Ground, would take Earthquake safely from the opposing Mega Garchomp.

Working through the types confirms Earthquake hits my Garchomp neutrally, and since their Garchomp has -2 Attack, that damage will be minimal while mine outspeeds decisively. That makes switching into Garchomp the clear choice here.

decisions.thought: Turn 3: My Garchomp (169 Spe) outspeeds their Mega Garchomp (100-158 Spe). Their Garchomp is at 87% with -2 Atk, -1 SpA, so its Earthquake is weakened. Mega Earthquake hits it for 2x and should KO or nearly KO. Incineroar (84 HP, Sitrus used) and Gholdengo stay in back. Unseen: Kingambit (Supreme Overlord), Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, Volcarona (Quiver Dance). Keep Gholdengo away from Earthquake users.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Our Garchomp is still at full health without mega evolving yet, while the opponent's Mega Garchomp is down to 87% with lowered Attack and Special Attack. Since both are Dragon/Ground type, Dragon-type moves like Dragon Claw would hit our Garchomp for super effective damage.

I'm weighing Dragon Claw against Earthquake: both would be super effective against the opponent's Dragon/Ground typing, but Earthquake has higher base power and our Garchomp's Attack stat should make it the stronger choice, so long as accuracy holds up.

decisions.thought: Opp Incineroar (41%, Sitrus used) has Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot. My Chomp at -2 Atk / -1 SpA; I Dragon Claw their Garchomp. Opp Chomp's EQ likely knocks out my Gholdengo and hurts Kingambit, so keep them out vs Chomp. If my Chomp falls, Kingambit (with an Attack boost from Supreme Overlord) cleans. One unseen opp mon is still to come: Gholdengo, Sinistcha, Corviknight or Dragapult.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: With my Chomp at -2 attack, I'm weighing whether opposing Garchomp has a speed boost that lets it outpace us with Dragon Claw or Outrage. I'm considering switching to Kingambit, but it's weak to Earthquake, so scarf Gholdengo might be safer since its 149 base speed with a Choice Scarf hits 223, likely outspeeding even a scarfed 169-speed threat.

decisions.thought: Opponent Mega Garchomp (sandforce) is at 35% with -2 Atk and -1 SpA. My Mega Garchomp is faster and at 105 HP. Dragon Claw is super effective on their Dragon/Ground Garchomp, so I'm using it to finish it. Their unrevealed threats are Kingambit (Supreme Overlord), Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, and Volcarona (Quiver Dance). Keep Gholdengo away from Earthquake users. Incineroar is at 84 HP with its Sitrus Berry used, so keep it in back.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Their Garchomp is down to 35% HP with lowered Attack, and I'm checking speed and typing matchups for my Mega Garchomp — working out whether Earthquake hits neutrally since their Garchomp is Dragon/Ground.

Dragon Claw is also fully accurate, so I'll go with it since Mega Evolution has already triggered.

decisions.thought: Opp Mega Chomp outsped my Mega Chomp (max speed) and its EQ did 96 damage. Plan: Chomp attacks and falls, then scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) Make It Rains their Chomp (about 56%, should KO). Kingambit gets Supreme Overlord boosts and cleans Incineroar (41%, Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot) and the last mon with Sucker Punch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since the opponent's Mega Garchomp outsped mine last turn, it'll KO me before I can act again, so staying is pointless. Switching to Kingambit seems better since Dark/Steel takes Ground super effectively but has solid bulk to survive their Earthquake.

Letting Chomp faint first boosts Kingambit's Supreme Overlord, though its Sucker Punch or Kowkazan Cleave might not quite secure the KO on their mega Chomp. A scarfed Gholdengo using Make It Rain could outspeed and hit hard enough to KO cleanly if it can switch in safely after Chomp goes down.

decisions.thought: Opp Mega Chomp (56%) is at least as fast as max-speed 158 and has EQ and Dragon Claw. Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) uses Make It Rain to KO it (about 110-130 damage, likely enough). Kingambit with Supreme Overlord then cleans Incineroar (41%, Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot) and the last mon with Sucker Punch. Watch for Incineroar Knock Off or Flare Blitz against Gholdengo.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With our Garchomp down, I need to pick a replacement. Mega Chomp is faster or speed-tied, but my Scarf Gholdengo outpaces it, so I'm calculating whether Make It Rain can do enough damage to Mega Chomp's special bulk.

Running the numbers, Make It Rain lands around 130 base damage after STAB, which should be enough to KO most of Mega Chomp's remaining health after rocks/prior damage, and it hits neutrally since Steel doesn't resist Dragon/Ground. Kingambit is tempting too since Garchomp's EQ is super effective on it, but Gholdengo seems like the safer, more reliable switch-in since this is a free switch after the faint.

decisions.thought: Opponent's Mega Garchomp is down. Their Gholdengo (goodasgold, possibly Life Orb) is now in. My Mega Garchomp (158 Spe) outspeeds it. Earthquake is super effective on Steel/Ghost Gholdengo and should do heavy damage. Gholdengo's special attacks threaten my 105 HP Garchomp, so if it survives, Earthquake again or switch to Gholdengo. Unseen: Kingambit, Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, Volcarona (Quiver Dance). Incineroar (84 HP, Sitrus used) stays in back.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo being Steel/Ghost makes it weak to Earthquake, and with Garchomp's high Attack that should deal heavy damage while outspeeding. I'm also considering Swords Dance as a setup option since Gholdengo can't inflict status to punish it.

Even so, Earthquake is the safer call since Gholdengo could retaliate hard with Make It Rain or Shadow Ball given its Special Attack with Life Orb, so hitting first with Earthquake is the right move.

decisions.thought: Scarf Gholdengo Make It Rain on opp Mega Chomp (56%, EQ/Dragon Claw) should KO. Then Kingambit (Supreme Overlord) cleans Incineroar (41%, Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot) and the last unseen mon (Gholdengo, Sinistcha, Corviknight or Dragapult). After Make It Rain, Gholdengo is at -2 SpA; switch to reset it if needed. Watch Incineroar Knock Off or Flare Blitz on Gholdengo.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: I'm checking whether a scarf Gholdengo outspeeds, then working out Make It Rain's damage against a mega Garchomp sitting around 56% HP, factoring in its special defense stat.

decisions.thought: Our Garchomp fainted to their Mega Garchomp's line and now their Gholdengo (goodasgold, -2 SpA, likely Life Orb) is active. Switching in our full-HP Gholdengo (Life Orb, Spe 149, possibly faster). Next turn, Thunderbolt is 2x on their Steel/Ghost Gholdengo; Shadow Ball is also 2x (Ghost vs Ghost). Avoid Make It Rain (resisted). Remaining unseen: Kingambit, Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, Volcarona (Quiver Dance). Keep Gholdengo away from Ground moves and Incineroar (84 HP, Sitrus used) for Fake Out/Parting Shot support later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Garchomp down, I can switch to Incineroar or Gholdengo. Their Gholdengo crit with Make It Rain and is at full health with Life Orb, outspeeding ours - I need to check if my Gholdengo's typing resists that Steel-type move.

Working through the matchup, Thunderbolt actually hits their Steel/Ghost Gholdengo for 2x since Electric crushes Steel, while Shadow Ball only gets neutral damage there - so bringing in Gholdengo and leading with Thunderbolt looks like the strongest play given their -2 SpA debuff weakening their returns.

decisions.thought: Opponent Gholdengo (goodasgold, -2 SpA from Make It Rain) is active at full HP. Our Gholdengo (Life Orb, 149 Spe) probably moves first or ties. Shadow Ball is super effective (Ghost vs Ghost) and gets STAB, so it's the strongest option. Don't use Make It Rain (resisted and self-debuffing). Remaining unseen: Kingambit, Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, Volcarona (Quiver Dance). Keep Incineroar (84 HP, Sitrus used) in back for Fake Out/Parting Shot later. Avoid Ground moves on Gholdengo.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Opponent's Gholdengo is already down to -2 SpA from Make It Rain, and I'm weighing whether Shadow Ball is the right call since it's super effective against their Ghost/Steel typing.

decisions.thought: Opp Gholdengo (moves unknown; possibly Focus Blast or Nasty Plot) and Incineroar (41%, Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, Sitrus used) remain. Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave beats their Gholdengo; Sucker Punch finishes. Keep my Scarf Gholdengo as backup (switching reset its SpA). Watch Incineroar re-Intimidate and Parting Shot.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: My Gholdengo is locked into Make It Rain at -2 SpA, which isn't great into their Gholdengo and leaves me vulnerable to a likely super-effective Shadow Ball. Switching to Kingambit looks safer since it resists both Shadow Ball and Make It Rain, though I need to watch out for Focus Blast, and Supreme Overlord would boost it if an ally has fainted.

Thunderbolt is 2x on its Steel half, so it is the best hit. Shadow Ball is resisted by Dark. Dark moves like Sucker Punch hit my Gholdengo hard (Ghost weakness). Remaining unseen: Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, Volcarona (Quiver Dance). Keep Incineroar (84 HP, no Sitrus) in back for Parting Shot / Fake Out later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Kingambit is at 73% HP and is Dark/Steel, so Thunderbolt hits for super effective damage while Shadow Ball is resisted. Thunderbolt is clearly the better option here.

decisions.thought: Opp Gholdengo (Life Orb, Shadow Ball, maybe Focus Blast) outspeeds Kingambit. Sucker Punch should KO before it moves; if they Nasty Plot or switch, use Kowtow Cleave next turn. Incineroar (41%, Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, Sitrus used) is last. My Scarf Gholdengo (full HP) is backup: Make It Rain/Shadow Ball. Kingambit has 7 Sucker Punch PP left after this.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: I'm calculating Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave damage against Gholdengo, factoring in the boost from a fainted ally, Black Glasses, STAB, and super effectiveness, working through the base damage formula with 205 attack against Gholdengo's defense before applying the multipliers.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: Last Incineroar (84/202, no Sitrus). Opposing Kingambit (73%, Atk -1 from Intimidate, SpD -1) has revealed Sucker Punch, and Supreme Overlord is active with 2 fainted allies. Flare Blitz is super effective on its Steel half and should do heavy damage. Sucker Punch is resisted by my Dark/Fire typing, so Incineroar can survive one hit. If Kingambit survives, next turn Flare Blitz again or Parting Shot is a fallback. Their remaining unseen threats are Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, and Volcarona (Quiver Dance).
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing whether to Flare Blitz the Kingambit, considering Steel resists Fire but checking how that interacts with its typing and current weakened state while my Incineroar is my last mon.

Incineroar at 84 HP needs to weigh Flare Blitz for the potential KO against the risk of Kingambit's Sucker Punch hitting first with boosted power from Supreme Overlord. Since Fake Out is off the table, I'm considering whether Protect might be safer to scout Kingambit's move before committing.

decisions.thought: Opp's last Pokémon: Incineroar at 41% (Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, Sitrus used). Switching to Scarf Gholdengo, then Focus Blast (super effective, should KO; 70% accuracy). Main threat to Gholdengo is Knock Off. Kingambit (73%, -1 Atk) is backup: Kowtow Cleave or Sucker Punch to finish a weakened Incineroar.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar just switched in, so Fake Out is still a threat this turn. Weighing a switch to Gholdengo — Make It Rain would be resisted by Fire typing, though Shadow Ball and Focus Blast have better coverage against Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing.

Checking Kingambit's damage with Kowtow Cleave at -1 attack plus Supreme Overlord and Black Glasses boosts — it's not enough to KO, while Incineroar's Flare Blitz back would likely kill Kingambit given the Fire weakness. Swords Dance is too risky if they Fake Out first then follow with Flare Blitz, so leaning toward evaluating whether Gholdengo eats a Fake Out safely as a Ghost-type.

If Incineroar Fake Outs Kingambit this turn instead, that actually enables a free Sucker Punch, though recalculating at -1 attack the Sucker Punch still falls short of a KO. Looking again at Gholdengo switching in, since Fake Out whiffs on Ghost types, Knock Off becomes the real threat to watch for.

Weighing the Focus Blast/Make It Rain coverage options against staying in with Kingambit, I'm leaning toward Gholdengo as the better switch overall, factoring in Incineroar's possible status moves. If I keep Kingambit in and eat the likely Fake Out, Kowtow Cleave chips them down, setting up a potential follow-up KO with Sucker Punch next turn before Flare Blitz lands.

Switching keeps Kingambit safe at 152 HP, and if they Fake Out on the switch it just whiffs. I'll go with Gholdengo here.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: Only Incineroar (30/202 HP, no Sitrus) remains. Opponent's last Pokemon is Kingambit (73%, Atk -1, SpD -1, Supreme Overlord active, Sucker Punch seen). Parting Shot is useless with no reserve to switch to. Protect only delays, since we have no healing and no Pokemon left to switch. Flare Blitz is super effective on Kingambit's Steel half and should KO or nearly KO it. Recoil may faint Incineroar, so this is a likely trade. Opponent's remaining unseen Pokemon are not in play.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar at low HP and Kingambit around 73%, I'm checking whether Flare Blitz's super effectiveness against Kingambit's Steel typing is enough to secure the knockout given its high Attack and Kingambit's solid Defense stat.

Since the recoil from Flare Blitz is a third of the damage dealt, and Incineroar's only sitting at 30 HP, that recoil alone could be fatal even if it lands the KO. Our team is down to just Incineroar, so Parting Shot isn't viable since there's nothing to switch into, leaving Flare Blitz or Protect as the real choices, though Protect just delays the inevitable since there's no way to heal up.

Either way Incineroar likely faints from recoil, so I'd lose if Kingambit survives. Could Protect help instead? Sucker Punch would fail against Protect, but that just delays things since opponent's Kingambit is their last Pokémon and Incineroar has no recovery — stalling with Protect doesn't change the outcome since Flare Blitz will eventually trigger the same lethal recoil at low HP.

There's a risk both faint simultaneously if Flare Blitz KOs Kingambit while recoil also KOs Incineroar, which could result in a tie rather than a win. Still, there's no way to reduce the recoil or guarantee survival, so going for Flare Blitz is the best option.

decisions.thought: Opponent's last mon is Incineroar at 14% (Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, Flare Blitz). Flare Blitz likely OHKOs Kingambit, so use Sucker Punch to get priority. If they used Parting Shot or another status move, follow with Kowtow Cleave next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit's Intimidate drop reset since it switched out and back in. Incineroar's at 14% with Supreme Overlord boosted to 1.2x from two fainted allies, and it moves first here. I'm weighing Flare Blitz, which hits Kingambit for super effective damage against its Steel typing despite being neutral on Dark, versus Sucker Punch as a safer option if Kingambit attacks.

Flare Blitz looks like it could outright KO Kingambit, which makes Sucker Punch essential if they go for an attacking move, since Fake Out won't work this turn and Kowtow Cleave means Incineroar would need to strike first anyway. The recoil from Flare Blitz would also likely finish off Incineroar given its low HP, raising the question of how Showdown resolves a double faint scenario, but Sucker Punch remains the clean, reliable play to secure the KO without that risk.
